# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 1, Chapter 4

**1** I saw a vision, brothers and sisters, twenty days after the former vision; a representation of the tribulation that is coming. **2** I was walking in the field road, and the distance from the public road is about ten stades. The place is very difficult of access. **3** While I was walking alone, I asked the Lord to bring to completion the revelations and visions which he had shown me through his holy church, in order to strengthen me and give repentance to all his servants who had stumbled, that his great and glorious name might be glorified, and because he thought me worthy to show me his marvels. **4** While I was glorifying him and giving thanks, something like the voice of a response came to me, "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." I began to reason in myself, "In what way can I be double-minded, after being established by the Lord, and after having seen such glorious things?" **5** And I went a little way forward, brothers and sisters. Behold, I saw dust rising up, as it were to heaven, and I began to say to myself, "Are cattle coming, raising a dust storm?" And it was about a stade away from me. **6** As the dust rose higher and higher, I suspected that it was something divine. The sun shone a little, and behold I saw a great beast like some Leviathan, and from its mouth fiery locusts were issuing forth. The beast was about a hundred feet in height and its head was like a vessel of earthenware. **7** And I began to weep and to pray to the Lord to rescue me from it. I recalled the word which I had heard, "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." **8** Thus, brothers and sisters, having put on faith in the Lord and called to mind the great and glorious things he had taught me, I took courage and faced the beast. Now the beast was coming with such a rush and force that it could have destroyed a city. **9** I came near it, and the great beast stretched itself out upon the ground and did nothing but put out its tongue; it never moved at all until I had passed by it. **10** Now the beast had upon its head four colors — black, then fiery and blood-red, then golden, then white.

---

*EMET note: "Leviathan" is the translator's identification based on beast description; Greek has "ketos" = sea-monster. "Stade" preserved as unit of measure (~185 meters).*
